question: True or false: the rods and cones of the eye pass on their light signals without firing nerve impulses?
answer: True. Rods and cones signal with graded shifts in voltage, and light makes them release less transmitter, not more: they release it most steadily in the dark. The first all-or-nothing spikes on the way to the brain appear two cells later, in the ganglion cells whose fibres bundle into the optic nerve.
move: The textbook case of a thing is rarely the only way it works.
trap: Assuming every nerve cell talks in spikes, as textbook neurons do.
source: Rodieck, The First Steps in Seeing, 1998
reference: Rodieck, The First Steps in Seeing, Sinauer Associates, 1998
